summary: Studies on-policy distillation (OPD) of small LLMs and finds that replacing the reverse-KL loss with a binary +1/-1 token reward pointing toward the teacher (BinaryOPD) trains about as well, and that only high-disagreement tokens' direction matters. Applies this to multi-teacher distillation (C-MOPD), supervising each sample with both a math and a code teacher, reporting gains over MOPD on math and function-level code benchmarks.

claims.claim: Binary directional reward reproduces OPD with reverse KL.
claims.evidence: §4.2 / Table 2 across five math student-teacher pairs and two code pairs (Table 1), Avg@8; comparable training curves. No repeated training seeds.

claims.claim: Only the direction of high teacher-student disagreement tokens is critical.
claims.evidence: §5.2 experiments flipping/ignoring low-disagreement tokens; App. E visualizations.

claims.claim: C-MOPD consistently outperforms MOPD on math and code.
claims.evidence: Table 5 (Qwen3-4B student, avg@8): LCB v6 32.9 vs 27.9, HumanEval 87.8 vs 85.9, MBPP 54.3 vs 53.5, AIME24 61.3 vs 60.0, MATH500 93.0 vs 92.9. Several gains are <1 pt with no training-seed variance; ε=0.8 picked from §5 findings rather than a held-out sweep. Single student model.

patterns.note: Post-training/distillation objective study; not about agent harnesses or agentic RL.

methodology.sample: Math: DAPO-Math-17k, DeepMath; code: Eurus; C-MOPD mixture of ~50k math/code problems. Evaluation on AIME24/25, AMC, MATH500, Minerva, OlympiadBench, LiveCodeBench v6, HumanEval, MBPP.
methodology.baselines: Standard OPD with reverse KL; MOPD for the multi-teacher setting. Appropriate but narrow.
methodology.models: 1.5B-30B students (DeepSeek-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, Qwen3-1.7B/4B/30B-A3B, Llama-3.2-3B); C-MOPD only on Qwen3-4B-Non-Thinking.
methodology.variance: Avg@8 sampling at evaluation; no repeated training runs or CIs.
methodology.ablations: Disagreement-threshold ε (0.0 vs 0.8), token-subset direction experiments, verifier alignment (App. B).
methodology.contamination_controls: None discussed; HumanEval/MBPP are widely contaminated benchmarks.
methodology.languages: Code benchmarks are Python function-level (HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench).

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint; extracted text shows an ICML-style warning, no acceptance stated.
standards.artifacts: Code at https://github.com/LeapLabTHU/KL-Free-OPD; hyperparameters in App. C.

biases.detail: Single training run per configuration; sub-point gains in Table 5 cannot be distinguished from noise.
Code evaluation limited to Python function-level benchmarks.
HumanEval and MBPP with no contamination analysis.
Model post-training objective; no agent, tool-use, or repository-level SE content.

coi.affiliations: LeapLab and Qiuzhen College, Tsinghua University; Beihang University; NUS; CUHK; E Fund Management Co., Ltd. (asset manager).
coi.detail: Industry co-authors are from a fund manager, not an AI vendor; no product evaluated.

verdict_reason: off-topic: LLM distillation loss study evaluated on math and Python function-level code benchmarks; it does not concern agents, harnesses, or repository-scale software engineering.
applicability: Does not transfer. A Java backend team building an agentic harness across ≥4 the repositories with mixed hosted agent hosts and spec-driven development does not distil models; the results are about training small open models and say nothing about Java, multi-repo work, or harness design.
